2611.17421.abstract: Electromagnetic observations have been the primary medium for studying cataclysmic variable (CV) systems, capitalizing on the invaluable opportunity they present to study binary stellar evolution and accretion. The launch of the Laser Interferometer Space Antenna (LISA) mission, however, will enable a multi-messenger perspective of the population. We extend previous work to explore the gravitational wave (GW) spectra sourced by a local and Galactic population of CVs. Using the Bayesian LISA Inference Package (BLIP), we simulate LISA data containing these CV populations to understand their impact and our ability to jointly model CV and double white dwarf (DWD) GW spectra. While we find that a local CV population has negligible effect on the LISA datastream, a Galactic CV population will have a signal-to-noise ratio of approximately 76, depending on the characteristics of the DWD population present, and will bias existing DWD spectral models if ignored. Current approaches struggle to accurately recover both populations' respective spectra, calling for the creation of multi-component spectral models that include GW contributions from both CVs and DWDs. These results point toward a promising future for the study of CVs with LISA.

2611.17519.abstract:
Unusually red L dwarfs (URLDs) probe extreme atmospheric conditions in the substellar regime, where enhanced dust opacity, cloud structure, and surface gravity effects challenge standard brown dwarf models. As free-floating analogues of young giant exoplanets, they provide key benchmarks for interpreting low-resolution infrared spectra from current and future wide-field space missions.
The goal is to identify new red L dwarf candidates both photometrically and spectroscopically in the first data release (DR1) of the Euclid space mission. The area covered is about 1,900 and 50 square degrees in the wide and deep survey, respectively.
We used colour cuts in multiple colour-colour diagrams combined with point-source and quality criteria to identify candidate red L dwarfs in both the Euclid wide and deep survey fields. We cross-matched photometric candidates with the SPHEREx mission and Euclid red grism spectra to confirm spectroscopic properties and evaluate bolometric magnitudes and colours.
We identified 1202 and 38 red L dwarf candidates in the Euclid wide and deep surveys, respectively. Spectroscopic follow-up and archival cross-matching confirm a substantial new population of red L dwarfs. Distance-independent diagnostics show that these objects occupy distinct loci characterised by enhanced condensate opacity and significant redness.
Euclid vastly expands the census of unusually red L dwarfs. While preliminary spectral classifications suggest many of these new candidates are intermediate-age (Pleiades-like) objects, a subset exhibits extremely red signatures indicative of very young, low-gravity (<=10 Myr) atmospheres, providing vital benchmarks for young exoplanet research.

2611.17590.abstract: We present a comprehensive analysis of the pulsating eclipsing binary HIP 7666 (TIC 308953703), containing a $\delta$ Sct-type component, based on 120-s TESS photometry and 63 newly acquired high-resolution echelle spectra. While previous orbital solutions were limited by sparse spectroscopic sampling, our extensive radial velocity (RV) measurements enable a robust determination of the system's physical parameters. The primary has an effective temperature of $T_{\rm eff,A}$ = 7376$\pm$72 K and a projected rotational velocity of $v_{\rm A}\sin i$ = 56.6$\pm$5.3 km s$^{-1}$. Joint modeling of the light and RV curves shows that HIP 7666 is a detached system in a circular orbit, with Roche-lobe filling factors of $f_{\rm A}$ = 57 \% and $f_{\rm B}$ = 44 \%. The masses and radii are determined to better than 2 \% precision: $M_{\rm A}$ = 1.822$\pm$0.029 $M_\odot$, $R_{\rm A}$ = 2.154$\pm$0.017 $R_\odot$ for the primary, and $M_{\rm B}$ = 1.246$\pm$0.020 $M_\odot$, $R_{\rm B}$ = 1.170$\pm$0.015 $R_\odot$ for the secondary. The binary-based distance (316$\pm$8 pc) agrees well with the Gaia DR3 parallax-based distance (313$\pm$1 pc), validating the derived system parameters. Frequency analysis of the light-curve residuals reveals 15 significant signals, predominantly in the $\delta$ Sct pulsation frequency range. PARSEC evolutionary tracks indicate an age of $\sim$0.9 Gyr and a supersolar metallicity ($Z=0.03$), with the primary on the main sequence and the secondary located close to the zero-age main sequence. Galactic kinematics place HIP 7666 in the thin disk.

2611.17628.abstract: The Vera C. Rubin Observatory's Legacy Survey of Space Time (LSST) is expected to discover numerous Mira variables in nearby galaxies, enabling their application for the cosmic distance scale. Miras are excellent distance indicators at infrared wavelengths, and therefore their period-luminosity (PL) relations in reddest $zy$ photometric systems will be crucial in the LSST era. We present first empirical $zy$-band PL relation for 85 oxygen-rich (O-rich) Miras located in the Large Magellanic Cloud based on time-series observations collected using the Dark Energy Camera (DECam) at the Víctor M. Blanco 4-m Telescope. The DECam photometry was directly calibrated using the Rubin Observatory Data Preview 2 (DP2) data. The observed PL relations were found to exhibit a break around a period of $\sim 300$ days, and therefore we only derived and calibrated the PL relations for Miras with a period shorter than $300$ days. We also explored the Rubin LSST DP2 data for known Mira variables in three Local Group dwarf galaxies. The $zy$-band light curves of Miras in IC 1613 are too sparsely sampled, whereas the DP2 observations of NGC 6822 and the Sagittarius Dwarf Irregular Galaxy cover only a short temporal baseline. For an O-rich Mira in NGC 6822, we obtain a distance modulus $\mu = 23.32\pm0.24$~mag in good agreement with the literature. Significantly improved temporal coverage is expected in the first official Rubin LSST data release that will enable a robust validation of the PL relation in these nearby systems.

2611.17665.abstract: Color--magnitude diagrams (CMDs) can constrain the progenitor masses of supernova remnants (SNRs), but mass estimates for massive stars are affected by limited temperature sensitivity, extinction, crowding, and nebular contamination. We use the Large Magellanic Cloud (LMC) SNR N63A and its OB association LH83 as a benchmark to evaluate CMD-based mass estimates. Among the tested diagnostics, the extinction-corrected MCPS $B$ vs. $U-B$ CMD provides the most useful constraint on the massive-star population. The $V$ vs. $B-V$ CMD is less reliable, while the reddening-free $W$-$Q$ diagram does not improve individual mass estimates because of its larger photometric uncertainties. Gaia EDR3 recovers bright stars missing or saturated in MCPS but provides weaker separation among the hottest stars. For seven spectroscopically classified stars, the $B$ vs. $U-B$ CMD-based masses are lower than the HR-diagram masses inferred using the same MIST tracks by $8.0~M_\odot$ on average, with a scatter of $7.0~M_\odot$. Isochrone comparisons suggest that most of the massive stars in LH83 formed about 7-15 Myr ago, complicating progenitor mass estimates based on the present-day mass function. Nevertheless, the masses of D243-1a and D243-2, stellar lifetimes predicted by the MIST models, and the empirical bubble-size-progenitor-mass relation suggest a progenitor mass of order 25-30 $M_\odot$. Our results highlight the potential and limitations of this approach for studying other LMC SNRs in OB associations.

2611.17807.abstract: The southward magnetic field carried by coronal mass ejections (CMEs) is a key driver of space weather events, yet how interacting CMEs amplify this field remains debated. The 10 May 2024 event, which produced the strongest geomagnetic storm since 2003, offers an ideal testbed for this question. Combining multi-spacecraft observations with high-resolution controlled numerical experiments, we track the CMEs continuously from their origin near the solar surface to beyond Earth, and find that inherent squeezing during CME-CME interactions generates the sustained enhancement of the southward field, exceeding 60 nT in magnitude near Earth. First driven by the dynamic pressure of the trailing CME and later maintained by magnetic and thermal pressures at the CME-CME interface, squeezing transforms the preceding CME from a bulky cloud into a flattened "pancake" structure, prevents expansion-induced field decay, and maintains an amplified southward field over long distances. The strength of this enhancement scales with the intensity of the squeezing. Our findings establish a direct link between CME-CME interaction and strong southward fields, laying a physics-based foundation for understanding and forecasting the geoeffectiveness of interacting CMEs.

2611.17838.abstract: Understanding the formation and evolution of dynamic fibrils (DFs) in active regions is essential for uncovering the physical processes operating in the highly structured and magnetized solar atmosphere. High-resolution chromospheric observations from the New Vacuum Solar Telescope (NVST) show DFs with periodic up-and-down motions. We carry out a statistical analysis of 176 DFs around a sunspot. The mean values of deceleration, maximum velocity, maximum length, and duration of the DFs are $120 \boldsymbol{\pm 43}~\mathrm{m~s^{-2}}$, $15.9 \boldsymbol{\pm 4.5}~\mathrm{km~s^{-1}}$, $1.13 \boldsymbol{\pm 0.48}~\mathrm{Mm}$, and $270 \boldsymbol{\pm 63}~\mathrm{s}$, respectively. Several pairs of parameters exhibit correlations, most notably a clear positive correlation between deceleration and maximum velocity. The consistency between the periodicities of DFs and running penumbral waves is first identified. We further find that DFs in regions with more vertical magnetic fields exhibit larger decelerations and shorter periods, whereas those in regions with more horizontal magnetic fields exhibit the opposite behavior. These results, together with the presence of running penumbral waves, support the interpretation that DFs are driven by slow magnetoacoustic waves. Furthermore, the multiwavelength signatures of DFs from the chromosphere to the corona imply a potential contribution to energy transport and heating in the solar atmosphere.

2611.17946.abstract: We present 3D radiative magnetohydrodynamic simulations of sunspots with a self-consistently generated penumbra. We analyze the impact of resolution, surrounding opposite-polarity fields and subsurface large-scale flows on the structure and stability of the simulated penumbra. Extended penumbral filaments are obtained for a subset of the simulations. These were run at 25 km (15 km) horizontal (vertical) resolution and with initial conditions favoring fields with strong horizontal components in the penumbral region. The surface velocities in these simulations are consistent with observations of Evershed flow. The main driving mechanism remains the same as illustrated previously in Rempel (2012). The most successful simulations produce extended penumbrae using a potential magnetic field top boundary, in contrast to previous simulations of extended penumbra with an artificial enhancement of horizontal magnetic field at the top boundary.

2611.17995.abstract:
Context. Blue stragglers are intriguing stars that appear more massive and younger than expected from single-star evolution, yet their evolutionary histories remain elusive because of the multiple possible formation channels. A promising and poorly explored avenue for addressing this problem is asteroseismology, which provides the most stringent constraints on internal structure and evolution.
Aims. We investigate five SX Phoenicis stars from the core of the globular cluster \omega Centauri that pulsate in two radial modes and occupy the blue-straggler region of the colour-magnitude diagram. Seismic models are constructed assuming a collisional origin and compared with our previous seismic studies based on single-star evolution. For comparison, we also explore a binary-evolution scenario involving mass transfer for one of the stars.
Methods. The evolution of the parent stars is computed with MESA. The collision is then modelled with the MMAMS code, which reconstructs the merger remnant using an entropic variable. The subsequent evolution is followed with MESA up to the current age of the cluster. Finally, we construct seismic models reproducing the observed frequencies of the two radial modes.
Results. We present the first seismic modelling of SX Phe stars (blue stragglers) based on the collision-formation scenario. Convective-core overshooting is essential for rejuvenation and for obtaining seismic models in the main-sequence phase of evolution, but it is not always sufficient. Whether a merger remnant undergoes rejuvenation depends in a complex way on the masses of the parent stars, metallicity, and collision time. We identify three evolutionary behaviours: no, delayed, and immediate rejuvenation. The collisional seismic models imply younger ages and higher masses than the seismic models based on single-star evolution.

2611.17997.abstract: We present a compact approximation to the dimensionless, volume-equivalent Roche lobe radius $R_{\rm L}/a$, obtained by applying symbolic regression to radii calculated from the full Roche potential. Over $10^{-5}\leq q\leq10^5$, the expression reduces the root mean square error from $1.97\times10^{-3}$ for Eggleton's formula to $5.95\times10^{-4}$, while its maximum relative error is $1.39\%$, compared with Eggleton's $0.83\%$. Calculations at additional mass ratios give a mean relative error of $0.331\%$. The formula is monotonic, recovers the $q^{\frac{1}{3}}$ scaling at small mass ratio, and approaches a large-mass-ratio limit within $0.036\%$ of the limiting Roche model. In a NumPy float64 benchmark of $10^7$ direct formula evaluations, the SR expression takes $0.217$~s compared with $0.450$~s for Eggleton, a speed-up of $2.08$. These results quantify the accuracy and evaluation cost of a compact algebraic alternative for binary-system calculations.

2611.18162.abstract: B supergiants are evolved massive stars with low surface gravities and lower effective temperatures, with substantial radiation-driven winds. Generally, they have been studied assuming 1D spherical symmetry. We present the first multi-D unified atmosphere and wind models for B supergiants, especially investigating the effects of approximate NLTE ionization and subsurface turbulence on the atmosphere and wind dynamics. We computed multi-D box-in-a-star RHD unified atmosphere and wind simulations of 2D/3D early B supergiant models using a hybrid opacity approach. We calculated line opacities from approximate NLTE populations, including line scattering. We calculated the flux-, energy-, and Planck-mean line opacities separately from our large line database using Sobolev escape probabilities, assuming two-level atoms. The models develop a highly turbulent atmosphere with time-averaged turbulent velocities of ~ 40 - 55 km/s at the photosphere in the 2D simulations, and ~ 25 km/s in 3D. In the cooler B1, B1.5 models, the wind acceleration is more gradual than in the hotter B0 model, leading to a significantly higher maximum wind speed in the B0 model. Further, the approximate NLTE formalism strongly alters the ionization stratification in the wind compared to LTE, modifying the line force. Mass-loss rates obtained in the models are of order 10^-6 - 3 x 10^-6 solar masses per year. Including turbulent pressure in hydrodynamically consistent NLTE CMF steady-state 1D simulations with comparable parameters can produce higher mass-loss rates and lower terminal wind velocities than in corresponding models without turbulent velocity, in overall qualitative agreement with our multi-D simulations. Our calculations suggest that in the lower surface-gravity B supergiants, in addition to modifying the photospheric density scale heights, turbulent pressure also influences global properties of the wind.

2611.18246.abstract: Auroral variability in ultracool dwarfs (UCDs) has been proposed as a key source of optical and infrared modulation, yet its physical origin remains poorly understood. We present JWST Near Infrared Imager and Slitless Spectrograph/Single Object Slitless Spectroscopy (NIRISS/SOSS) time-series spectroscopy of the M8.5 UCD LSR J1835+3259. These observations probe the object's wavelength-dependent rotational variability, providing insight into the atmospheric processes underlying its infrared behaviour. Additional GTC/MEGARA optical spectra reveal that its H$\alpha$ emission has declined markedly since earlier epochs, suggesting a reduced activity state during the JWST observations. We detect no emission from H$_3^+$ or absorption by hydronium in the NIRISS spectra. We use principal component analysis to identify two distinct modes of spectral variability: one dominated by FeH modulation near 1 $\mu$m and another contributing broadband variability across the H and K bands. We find that no model atmosphere grid provides a reasonable fit to the average NIRISS spectrum. However, a blended model comprising an M-dwarf photosphere and a cooler blackbody component provides an improved fit to the mean spectrum, the broadband spectral energy distribution and the NIRISS broadband variability. By adding perturbations to PICASO model grids, we demonstrate that a combination of atmospheric heating and non-equilibrium chemistry can successfully mimic a blend of unperturbed photosphere and a blackbody, and that the presence of these effects may explain the unusual spectrum and variability of LSR J1835+3259.

2611.18254.abstract: Variability of massive stars indicates the presence of complex, multi-D physics near the surface. Recent advancements in multi-D radiation-hydrodynamical modelling of massive star atmospheres show strong turbulence triggered by the iron opacity bump. We analyze statistical properties of sub-surface turbulence in multi-D simulations of O-star atmospheres. Particularly, we study potential dependencies of turbulent properties on global stellar parameters. Using 2D O-star models, we studied several statistical properties of the turbulence that develops in these models. We compute autocorrelation functions of density and velocity to study typical eddy length scales. Moreover, we compute kinetic energy power spectra to analyze the energy distribution and compare this to known results from established turbulence theories. We find anisotropy of the turbulent eddies in velocity space. Moreover, this anisotropy increases with classical Eddington factor. This anisotropy disappears in density space where all models show nearly isotropic structures and no dependence on stellar parameters. The kinetic energy power spectra exhibit an inertial range with a cascade exponent that has an average value of -2.57. This exponent does not show any clear dependence on stellar parameters. Importantly, this energy cascade is significantly steeper than those in known turbulence theories such as Kolmogorov turbulence with exponent -5/3 and Burgers turbulence with exponent -2. This additional steepening can potentially be attributed to radiative damping which increases with increasing wavenumber. Sub-surface turbulence in hot, massive stars is anisotropic and radially dominated in velocity space and its energy cascade is steeper than both Kolmogorov turbulence and Burgers turbulence. Although not rigorously proven here, we suggest that this steepening is due to the scale-dependent effect of radiative damping.

2611.18310.abstract: The surface magnetic field of the young solar analogue V889 Her is studied using Zeeman-Doppler imaging (ZDI). This well-studied star has previously been reported to have an exceptionally high differential rotation and show abrupt changes in the surface magnetic field and spot configuration. Our aim is to study the evolution of the magnetic field topology in V889 Her. This will contribute to understanding dynamo action in young solar-type stars. We also want to constrain the surface differential rotation curve of the target this http URL. We employ the ZDI method on observations collected with the SOFIN spectropolarimeter mounted at the Nordic Optical Telescope. We test differential rotation parameters previously reported in studies of the star. We observe significant changes in the radial field near the rotational pole throughout the whole span of the observations. Specifically, the polarity of the radial field is reversed around 2021. The large-scale magnetic field also contains a persistent strong azimuthal component at high latitudes. We detect abrupt changes in the spot configuration in June 2018 on the time scale of a week. The observations favour a solar type differential rotation. The different rotation parameters influence the brightness map more than the magnetic field topology. We cannot link the observed changes in the magnetic field topology with the evolution of the long-term spot activity. The abrupt changes observed in 2018 confirm previous reports that the surface magnetic field and spot configuration may undergo rapid evolution on short time scales. This complicates the estimation of the surface differential rotation.

2611.18326.abstract: Recent white-light observations from the Metis coronagraph on board Solar Orbiter have shown the presence of propagating density fluctuations with a period of $\sim5$ minutes, particularly in the observationally bright regions of helmet streamers and pseudo-streamers. These density fluctuations have been shown to originate from magnetohydrodynamic wave modes -- slow and fast modes can directly compress the plasma, whereas Alfvén waves generate density fluctuations via a non-linear coupling with the slow and fast modes. In general, in low plasma $\beta$ regions, slow modes contribute more towards the generation of density fluctuations, whereas in high $\beta$ regions, there are significant contributions from both slow and fast waves. In this work, we investigate the propagation of (non-linear) Alfvén waves and the associated density fluctuations using a 2.5D axisymmetric global solar wind model that includes two distinct magnetic field topologies -- a helmet streamer and a pseudo-streamer. Key differences in these magnetic configurations give rise to differences in the wave behaviour due to, for example, the presence of a current sheet in the helmet streamer and an X-type null point in the pseudo-streamer, and the structure of the $\beta = 1$ layer in both magnetic field configurations. This leads to the possible creation of prominent interference patterns along the helmet streamer axis, which do not appear along the pseudo-streamer axis. Unlike in the streamer region, we also find that along the pseudo-streamer axis, the contribution to the density fluctuations is due to the fast waves only, despite being in a low $\beta$ plasma.

2611.17410.abstract: Most of the hundred million stellar-mass black holes (BHs) expected in the Milky Way are predicted to be isolated. Characterizing this BH population will provide insights into stellar evolution and supernova explosion physics. The Nancy Grace Roman Space Telescope Galactic Bulge Time Domain Survey (GBTDS) will enable the detection of isolated BHs through astrometric microlensing, apparent stellar position shifts caused by deflection of distant starlight. We combine a Galactic model, stellar population synthesis model, BH initial--final mass relation, and kick velocity distribution to simulate events caused by isolated BH lenses. We assess the expected yield, sensitivity, characterization potential, and signal characteristics of these events to inform GBTDS search strategies. We predict $487 \pm 37$ isolated-BH microlensing events with detectable astrometric signals, 82% of which have impact parameters beyond 2 Einstein radii and consequently have small or undetectable photometric signals. Standard astrometric fits yield unit weight errors > 1.2 for 18% and > 2 for 2% of these events. Sensitivity peaks for 5-6$M_\odot$ BHs and is limited by the five-year GBTDS baseline. Weak microlensing parallax constraints limit BH mass precision, but events with Einstein timescales > 100 days and angular Einstein radii > 1.2 mas have high BH lens probabilities within our Galactic model. Wide-separation astrometric microlensing offers an independent discovery channel for isolated BHs beyond photometrically selected events. Realizing this opportunity requires dedicated multi-season GBTDS searches, joint astrometric and photometric modeling, and accounting for other astrometric variability. Although precise individual masses are challenging for these events, probabilistic lens classification could lead to Galactic abundance constraints on the population of isolated BHs.

2611.17423.abstract: The architectures of planetary systems encode their formation and dynamical histories. In the Solar System, the near alignment of planetary orbits, the Kuiper Belt, and the Sun's equator supports planet formation in a rotating disk of gas and dust. However, some exoplanet systems show planets on orbits misaligned with their host stars or other planets, raising the question of whether misalignments are primordial or produced by post-formation dynamics. We present the first population-level constraints on the mutual inclinations of 32 planets in 16 systems relative to debris disks. We find that planets across orbital distances from 0.1 to 100 AU are predominantly aligned with the debris disks within 10 deg (30/32 planets). The alignment holds across systems spanning tens of million years to a few gigayears in age. These results indicate that the aligned architecture of the Solar System is representative of the birth conditions of exoplanet systems.

2611.17430.abstract: The central compact object (CCO) 1E 1207.4-5209 is remarkable in that its X-ray spectrum shows clear absorption features at ~0.7 and 1.4 keV. Attributing these features to electron cyclotron resonance, the implied surface magnetic field is B~(7-8)x10^10 G, which agrees approximately with the field inferred from the spin properties of the pulsar. Here we examine all XMM-Newton EPIC pn spectra from more than 30 observations of 1E 1207.4-5209 from 2001-2020. We model the rotation phase-averaged and phase-resolved spectra with a two blackbody and multiple absorption line model, focusing on potential changes in the absorption lines which would correspond to changes in the magnetic field that could be related to the pulsar's possible spin glitch in 2015 and recent detection in radio. We find the phase-averaged spectral parameters, and by implication the magnetic field, are constant across nearly 20 years of data, while some parameters characterizing the phase-resolved spectra vary with rotation phase. The spectral line energies and widths (e.g., E_1~0.66 keV and full width of 0.34 keV) imply the magnetic field distribution across the X-ray emitting regions spans the range B~(6-11)x10^10 G, with the highest fields being visible during the declining phase of the pulsations of 1E 1207.4-5209.

2611.17651.abstract: The detection of solar neutrino provides direct evidence for on-going fusion in the core of the Sun and serve as a probe for that solar core. Production rate of $^8$B is sensitive to the solar core temperature. Adiabatic flavor conversion of $^8$B solar neutrinos depends on the local solar electron density. Combined with the roughly exponential decrease in solar electron density with increasing distance from the center of the solar sphere, the solar core size, density, and temperature are inferred. This article presents an outer bound on solar core size and measurements of the density and temperature in the solar core based on Super-Kamiokande phase I-IV solar neutrino data. An outer bound is set for the solar core at $90\%$ confidence level as $0.499R_\odot$ for the high metallicity B16+GS98 Standard Solar Model and $0.381R_\odot$ for K2-A09-MZvar-12 which includes protosolar accretion. A combined fit with the SNO polynomial coefficients improves the limit to $0.268R_\odot$ for B16+GS98 and $0.215R_\odot$ for K2-A09-MZvar-12. Results for other metallicity cases are also reported. In the high metallicity scenario assuming nominal solar core density and solar core size, temperature at the solar center is reported at $T_\text{C}=(15.599\pm0.0016)\times10^6$ K and $T_{\text{npz}}=(15.492\pm0.0017)\times10^6$ K at the peak radius of the $^8$B production profile.

2611.18314.abstract: Collisionless shocks are primary sites of particle acceleration throughout the Universe. Transient, mesoscale structures forming around these shocks influence their energy conversion efficiency, yet remain poorly observed at interplanetary (IP) shocks: spacecraft sample the shock transition briefly, and single-point measurements cannot disentangle temporal evolution from spatial structure. Here, we examine a fast, CME-driven IP shock of 2026 January 19, observed by IMAP, SOLAR-1, Wind, ACE, DSCOVR, and Aditya-L1 at L1 and by ARTEMIS and MMS near Earth, to determine its spatial and temporal structure. At MHD scales, a pre-existing solar wind flux tube is overtaken by the shock as it crosses the L1 fleet. This inflates the apparent magnetic compression ratio far beyond the ideal strong-shock limit of 4, showing that upstream and downstream intervals can sample different plasma and bias single-spacecraft estimates. At kinetic scales, IMAP and SOLAR-1, separated by only $\sim$7 $R_E$ ($\sim$340 ion inertial lengths), sample the same foreshock yet record localized structures that differ measurably; these are the first candidate signatures of large-scale foreshock transients at an IP shock. Further upstream, shocklets appear hundreds of $R_E$ ahead of the shock, consistent with steepening of ambient solar wind waves. Near Earth, the shock-to-flux-tube arrival lag increases to approximately six minutes, corresponding to a nominal sheath extension of $\sim$50 $R_E$, indicating sheath expansion over $\sim$200 $R_E$ of propagation. Together, these results show that the IP shock, its foreshock, and its sheath evolve across multiple scales from L1 to Earth, underscoring the need for multipoint measurements to resolve the underlying processes.
